title: GUI-WEdit and GUI-SkillEvo: Gradient-Free Adaptation of Small GUI Agents
read_level: full (PDF v1 via pdftotext; no HTML version exists; 5-page technical report, Figure 1 as caption only)
metadata_mismatch: none in title/authors; the PDF body states "Date: November 16, 2026" while arXiv v1 is dated 24 Nov 2026
why_wsp: For the 4B model, an unspecified 'research assistant' diagnoses OSWorld failures from trajectories and a fixed equality-constrained closed-form solve (gradients disabled, no optimizer) computes the update to one late MLP down_proj; the paper cites WSP as motivation but does not say an LLM determines the weight values, and the 2B route edits skill text, not weights.
editor: 4B: closed-form constrained solve (Eq. 2); targets chosen from diagnosed failures by a 'research assistant' / 'development assistant' that is not named. Paper: "Weight-space programming motivates using a language-model assistant to inspect failures and implement targeted changes to model parameters [3, 4]. Our implementation uses supervised state-action evidence and a constrained closed-form solve." (Sec 1). 2B: assistant drafts skills, weights fixed.
target: GUI-Owl-1.5-4B-Instruct, layer 35 mlp.down_proj (2560 x 9728); GUI-SkillEvo uses GUI-Owl-1.5-2B-Instruct with weights unchanged
interface: closed form ("Delta W = U (K^T C^-1 K)^-1 K^T C^-1", Eq. 2, with guard bank of successful states)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (candidates screened on guard residuals then evaluated in closed-loop desktop interaction; earlier accepted edits retained)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "An elementwise audit against the original backbone found 23,739,095 changed values in this single tensor out of 4,437,815,808 total parameter values (0.5349%). The other 712 serialized tensors are identical." (Sec 2.1)

headline_results.where: Table 2 (historical base / final / difference / full score)

headline_results.quote: Against the historical 4B reference, 38 tasks improve, 20 decrease, and 303 retain the same score.
The final construction stage used one target input and 812 guard inputs, yielding 34,707 protected token states

baselines_and_controls: Historical project reference scores of the unedited backbones only ("Historical backbone test scores are included for reference"); no fine-tuning, random-edit, or prompting baselines.
runs_and_variance: single run / not reported (greedy decoding, temperature 0; one final evaluation per system)
robustness_of_edits: Construction accounts for BF16 rounding: "account for BF16 rounding and the configured repetition penalty in token checks, and reject candidates that violate the declared checks after serialization" (Sec 2.1). No fine-tuning or quantization survival tests.
verification: Elementwise checkpoint audit against original backbone; guard-state constraints; no formal verification.
limitations_stated: None stated in a dedicated section; paper describes itself as "an engineering study of a feedback-driven adaptation workflow".
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog) [3]
Zhang, Wang, Lin, Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?, arXiv 2611.09376 [4]
notes_for_survey: Cites WSP as motivation but the 4B weight values come from a ROME-like equality-constrained closed-form solve over guard and target activations; whether an LLM picks the target states is not stated (only an unnamed 'research assistant'). Baseline is a historical reference score, not a re-run of the unedited model in the same harness. The 2B half is prompt/skill evolution with frozen weights and is not WSP.
